Chris Johnson

Director, Scientific Computing and Imaging Institute
University of Utah
sci.utah.edu

Biomedical Computing and Visualization

In this talk I will present recent research results in computational neuroscience and imaging within the context of an interactive problem solving environment (BioPSE/SCIRun) for biomedical applications. As opposed to the typical "off-line" simulation mode - in which the scientist manually sets input parameters, computes results, visualizes the results via a separate visualization package, then starts again at the beginning - BioPSE "closes the loop" and allows interactive steering of the design, computation, and visualization phases of the simulation. I will provide examples of several driving applications of steering and interactive visualization in neuroscience (new inverse source localization techniques and surgical planning), and imaging (new methods for interactive visualization of large-scale 3D MRI and CT volumes, and introduce new methods for diffusion tensor imaging).
